answer: Pedersen DKG lets a group jointly generate a public key with no dealer and no trusted setup, and the orchard of the protocol is that every participant contributes randomness and proves its share is consistent. The trellis of the design is a complaint round where bad shares are exposed and the culprit removed, so a Sybil clique cannot poison the key. The resulting key belongs to the whole group, and a pigment of independent participants must cooperate to sign, which makes one person with many accounts no stronger than one person.
